text.p: Following are some of the major events to have occurred on October 1 in history.
1207 - Henry III, King of England 1216-72, born.
1684 - Pierre Corneille, French playwright who wrote "Le Cid", died aged 78.
1754 - Paul I, Emperor of Russia 1796-1801 and successor to Catherine the Great, born.
1795 - Belgium became part of the French Republic.
1865 - Paul Dukas French composer born. Best known for "The Sorcerer's Apprentice" which featured on the soundtrack of the Disney film "Fantasia".
1904 - Vladimir Horowitz born. He was one of history's great concert pianists and was also Arturo Toscanini's son-in law.
1904 - Austrian physicist Otto Robert Frisch born. He was responsible for work on the uranium atom which led to the development of the atomic bomb.
1908 - Henry Ford's Model T Ford went on sale for the first time.
1910 - Bonnie Parker, famed for her four-year crime spree with Clyde Barrow in the U.S. southwest that resulted in at least 12 murders, born.
1914 - Turkey closed the Dardenelles to the allies in World War One.
1918 - Arab forces assisted by the British under T. E. Lawrence captured Damascus from the Turks.
1923 - Southern Rhodesia became a self-governing colony within the British Commonwealth.
1924 - James Earl (Jimmy) Carter born. The 39th president of the United States (1977-81), he was defeated in the subsequent election by Ronald Reagan.
1928 - Stalin's first Five-Year Plan which set targets for every industry, factory and workshop went into operation in the Soviet Union.
1936 - General Francisco Franco was named head of the Nationalist Government in Spain.
1938 - German troops crossed into the Sudetenland following an agreement between Britain, France, Germany and Italy to avoid war over Czechoslovakia.
1943 - After a month-long battle, allied soldiers captured Naples in Italy.
1946 - The International War Crimes Tribunal in Nuremburg sentenced 12 Nazi leaders to death.
1949 - The People's Republic of China was formed with Mao Zedong as its head.
1960 - The Federation of Nigeria achieved independence within the Commonwealth. It became a federal republic in 1963, also on October 1.
1962 - The United Nations took control of West New Guinea (now Irian Jaya) from the Netherlands.
1964 - Japan's "bullet train" from Tokyo to Osaka made its first journey.
1965 - A coup attempt in Indonesia was crushed by an army officer named Suharto, who became president two years later.
1966 - Nazi leaders Albert Speer and Baldur von Schirach were released from Spandau prison in Berlin, leaving Rudolf Hess the sole prisoner.
1969 - The Anglo-French Concorde aircraft broke the sound barrier for the first time in a test flight over France.
1969 - Olaf Palme was elected leader of the Social Democratic Party and Swedish Prime Minister.
1974 - The Watergate cover-up trial opened in Washington.
1979 - The Panama Canal Zone was formally handed over to Panama after 70 years of U.S. control.
1982 - Helmut Kohl was sworn in as West Germany's sixth Chancellor, succeeding Helmut Schmidt.
1987 - Fiji coup leader Colonel Sitiveni Rabuka formally revoked his country's constitution, saying he had replaced Queen Elizabeth as head of state with power to rule by decree.
1989 - Pakistan rejoined the Commonwealth after a 17-year absence.
1991 - President Aristide of Haiti flew into exile in Venezuela after a coup by a three man military junta led by General Raul Cedras.
1995 - France carried out the second in its series of nuclear weapons tests at Fangataufa atoll in the South Pacific.

1995 - U.S. federal jury found Egyptian cleric Sheikh Omar Abdel-Rahman and nine others guilty of plotting to blow up the World Trade Centre, bomb the United Nations, kill Egypt's president and destroy vital highway tunnels in New York.
